title: This week's notable physics papers on arXiv

sections.title: JWST Excludes Exomoons Down to 0.1 Earth Radii Around a Rocky, Temperate Exoplanet
sections.abstract: Using twelve JWST transits of LP 890-9c, the author finds no exomoon and excludes moons larger than 0.1 Earth radii at 95% confidence across the Hill region.
sections.claimed_result: The paper claims the most sensitive exomoon search so far and demonstrates JWST sensitivity to moons near 0.1 Earth radii.
sections.caveat: The close-in orbit makes large moons unlikely to survive for gigayears; one epoch had red noise.

sections.title: A photonic source with half-a-GHz single-photon flux
sections.abstract: A deterministic source delivers more than 500 MHz of in-fibre single-photon flux.
sections.claimed_result: The source exceeds 500 MHz in-fibre flux and produces over 100 pW optical power.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not give the full purity-efficiency-stability tradeoff.

sections.title: Microkelvin resolution thermometry at the nanometre scale
sections.abstract: Dual-NV nanodiamonds and a quantum-sensing chip yield 682 microkelvin measurement error and below-50 mK/sqrt(Hz) sensitivity.
sections.claimed_result: The work improves nanoscale thermometry sensitivity by about an order of magnitude.
sections.evidence_basis: NV nanodiamond thermometry and controlled heating tests.
sections.caveat: The optical probe itself heats the sample.

sections.title: Fast Bayesian Inference for Long-Duration Gravitational-Wave Signals in 3G detectors
sections.abstract: A decomposition and relative-binning scheme accelerates inference for a 21.3-hour signal by about four orders of magnitude.
sections.claimed_result: The method makes day-long 3G signal inference practical.
sections.evidence_basis: Waveform likelihood evaluation for a simulated long-duration signal.
sections.caveat: Broader waveform families and realistic nonstationary noise still need validation.

sections.title: Percent-Level Prediction of the Deuteron Magnetic Polarizability
sections.abstract: An NNLO pionless-EFT calculation predicts the deuteron magnetic polarizability with 1.3% uncertainty.
sections.claimed_result: The result is 0.0789 +/- 0.0010 fm^3, reducing the prior uncertainty from 4.9%.
sections.evidence_basis: NNLO EFT calibrated with the thermal np to d gamma rate.
sections.caveat: It remains a theory prediction requiring independent cross-checks.

sections.title: Early against Late: A contrast on dark energy in the light of DESI DR2
sections.abstract: Bayesian comparison of early- and late-time dark-energy models against Lambda-CDM disfavors both extensions.
sections.claimed_result: The paper reports strong rejection of EDE with CMB data and moderate disfavoring of CPL.
sections.evidence_basis: Bayesian model comparison using DESI-era, supernova, and CMB data.
sections.caveat: Results depend on priors, likelihoods, and model parameterization.

sections.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
sections.abstract: The paper models inelastic xenon excitation accompanying dark-matter interpretations of the LZ high-recoil event.
sections.claimed_result: The companion rate is often about 0.1 of the elastic rate or smaller.
sections.evidence_basis: NREFT, shell-model transitions, detector simulation, and a schematic background model.
sections.caveat: The event is isolated and the background model is simplified; this is not a dark-matter detection.

sections.title: Higgs Boson Pair Production via Gluon Fusion: Higher-Order Corrections and Theoretical Uncertainties
sections.abstract: An LHC Higgs Working Group report updates higher-order corrections and uncertainty recommendations for gluon-fusion Higgs-pair production.
sections.claimed_result: It consolidates QCD, electroweak, mass-scheme, and scale uncertainties for gg to hh predictions.
sections.evidence_basis: Perturbative collider calculations and uncertainty assessment.
sections.caveat: It is a theory update, not a new Higgs-pair observation.
